title_by_locale.hi: हमारे आस-पास की वस्तुओं का अवलोकन
सामग्रियों को समूहों में कैसे बाँटें?
जिन सामग्रियों के आर-पार देखा जा सकता है

notes: Objects around us; materials used for a tumbler; balls of different materials and bounce comparisons; sorting objects; visibility through materials; soluble/insoluble materials (panels a/b); a cup on a balance; tumblers with different water levels (panels a/b).
Other inline photographs/illustrations and possible numbering/layout differences must be checked against rendered PDFs.
Predictions/observations from mixing materials with water

items: Think about suitable material for a tumbler and cooking utensils
Compare bounce heights of same-size balls made from different materials dropped from a fixed height
Observe hard/soft objects and identify materials
Test sugar, salt, chalk powder, sand and sawdust in water after stirring and waiting
Compare mass using identical cups half-filled with water, sand and pebbles on a balance

unnumbered_investigations: Sort paper, cardboard, wood, chalk, copper wire, aluminium foil and alloys by shine, texture and colour.
Discuss whether water is transparent and whether it can be made opaque.
Observe different water levels in identical tumblers and connect occupied space with volume.
sidebars_and_special_notes: Pottery-making: clay selection/preparation, shaping and firing
Traditional/Ayurvedic classification using pairs of properties
Think it over: changes introduced by plastic and whether they are a benefit or drawback
Non-lustrous examples include paper, wood, rubber and jute; polishing/coating can make surfaces shiny, and not all shiny objects are metals
Hardness can be compared through resistance to compression/scratching and is relative (rubber compared with sponge and iron)
ORS and dissolving context; learner content should direct actual ORS use to packet/health-worker guidance
Some liquids form separate layers; oxygen can dissolve in water
Mass and weighing: everyday speech may call it weight, but the section introduces mass
Volume units: L/mL for common liquid labels; SI cubic metre m³; 1 m³ = 1000 L
Unit notation: kg lowercase, mL lowercase m plus uppercase L, no space inside unit symbols, space between number and unit

tasks: Find the companion: connect related words such as iron, transparent, copper, solid, bottle, plastic, lustrous, wood, opaque and glass.

True/false on transparency, lustre, solubility and matter
Choose materials for chairs based on desired properties
Choose containers for food waste, broken glass and wastepaper
Classify air and wooden door by transparency
Infer properties of mysterious materials X and Y
Identify materials from riddles and write a new riddle
Pair provided liquids/solids by soluble/insoluble behaviour
